content: Notch 1, also referred to as NOTCH1, is a human gene that encodes a single-pass transmembrane receptor. This receptor is a member of the Notch family, which consists of Type 1 transmembrane proteins. These proteins share structural features, including an extracellular domain with multiple epidermal growth factor-like (EGF) repeats and an intracellular domain composed of various distinct domain types. Members of the Notch family are critical in numerous developmental processes by regulating cell fate decisions. The Notch signaling pathway is an evolutionarily conserved intercellular communication system that governs interactions between adjacent cells. In Drosophila, the interaction of Notch with its cell-bound ligands, such as Delta and Serrate, establishes a signaling pathway essential for development. While homologues of these ligands have been identified in humans, the precise interactions between these ligands and human Notch homologues remain to be fully elucidated. The Notch 1 protein undergoes cleavage in the trans-Golgi network and is presented on the cell surface as a heterodimer. It functions as a receptor for membrane-bound ligands and is thought to play multiple roles during development. A deficiency in Notch 1 has been associated with bicuspid aortic valve formation. There is evidence that activated Notch 1 and Notch 3 promote the differentiation of progenitor cells into astroglia. When Notch 1 is activated prenatally, it induces the differentiation of radial glia, whereas postnatal activation leads to differentiation into astrocytes. One study suggests that the Notch-1 signaling cascade is activated by Reelin through an unidentified mechanism. Additionally, Reelin and Notch 1 cooperate in the development of the dentate gyrus. NOTCH1 has been shown to interact with several proteins, including: GSK3B (Glycogen Synthase Kinase 3 Beta), Lck (Lymphocyte-specific protein tyrosine kinase), MAML1 (Mastermind-like protein 1), Mothers against decapentaplegic homolog 3 (SMAD3), NFKB1 (Nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells 1), NOV (Nephroblastoma overexpressed gene), RBPJ (Recombination signal binding protein for immunoglobulin kappa J region), SNW1 (SNW domain-containing protein 1), Ubiquitin C, and YY1 (Yin Yang 1).
